referenced_urls.title: From Voiceprints to User Entities: Online Speaker-Memory...

relevance: Memory design for voice agents serving several people.

media.description: Abstract excerpt introducing EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free speaker-memory layer for personalized spoken agents, and the LoCoMo-ID spoken-memory benchmark.
media.ocr_text: Personalized spoken agents must identify speakers before accessing user-specific memory, yet memory benchmarks typically assume correctly attributed histories. We argue that voiceprints are observations of identity, not identities themselves, and formulate online speaker-memory construction to maintain persistent user entities as acoustic evidence evolves. We introduce EvoSpeakerMem, a training-free layer for causal speaker routing, selective acoustic-state updates, and identity-partitioned memory writes and retrieval through a replaceable text-memory backend. We also construct LoCoMo-ID, a spoken-memory benchmark with hidden speaker identities, speaker-sensitive queries, simulated recording-condition shifts, and four-speaker identity-confusion tests.
